clue.text: False part of expert's research paper

parts.note: a pro is an expert, here with the possessive 's
a thesis is a dissertation written up from research

explanation.surface: Someone questions which part of a specialist's research paper might be fabricated.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part, such as a false limb or tooth.

clue.text: Managed, say, to climb several mountains?

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example', i.e. say

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone succeeded in scaling a series of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a connected line or chain of mountains.

clue.text: Section of head exposed at the front with large surgical tool

parts.note: the scalp is the skin covering the top of the head

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of exposed
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A grisly operating-theatre picture of part of a head laid bare by a big instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the small, very sharp knife used by surgeons.

clue.text: How silly of me to overturn this carrying trough

indicators.note: overturning a down entry flips it so its letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: doh is the exclamation used when one realises one has been stupid

explanation.surface: Someone berates themselves for clumsily tipping over a builder's carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doh!' is Homer Simpson's cry of self-reproach. A hod is the open box on a pole that builders use to carry bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod is a builder's open trough on a long handle for carrying bricks or mortar.

clue.text: Times spent inside for physio exercises?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: prison terms, in slang
second meaning: movements that lengthen muscles

explanation.surface: Sessions spent indoors doing the routines a physiotherapist prescribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like indoors, but it is slang for in prison; a stretch is a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is both a prison sentence in slang and a muscle-lengthening exercise a physiotherapist prescribes.

clue.text: Harmonise initial elements of sound, yet nothing's clearly heard

indicators.note: the initial element of each word is its opening letter, so those are taken in turn

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Advice to a sound engineer: line things up so that nothing can be heard distinctly.
explanation.definitionFit: To synch is to make things coincide in timing, as sound with film, so they operate together.

clue.text: Training programme is rough, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: coarse means rough in texture

explanation.surface: Word has it that a particular training scheme is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a series of lessons or a set programme of study or training.

clue.text: Advanced nursing staff may be found here

definitions.text: nursing staff may be found here
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: located in a hospital room

explanation.surface: A note on where senior nurses are posted in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer as ON WARD: nurses are often on a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Onward is an adjective meaning moving forward, as advanced does in the sense of having progressed.

clue.text: Irregular stuff inspires core of nationalist party

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word takes the others inside it

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here the middle of an eleven-letter word

parts.note: the sixth of eleven letters is the centre one
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An erratic piece of writing that motivates the heart of a nationalist movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means haphazard, without a pattern, so not following any regular order.

clue.text: Quickly look around tower in a castle

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick glance

explanation.surface: A tourist told to take a swift glance around a castle's main tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest, innermost tower of a medieval castle.

clue.text: Flawed protagonist — one featuring in another novel

indicators.note: featuring in something means appearing within it, so one piece goes inside the other
novel means new, so the letters take on a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lead character with flaws who turns up in a second book as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book in the surface, which suits the protagonist, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character who lacks conventional heroic virtues, so is a flawed protagonist.

clue.text: Guys in a fix ultimately sought change

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the rest

parts.note: a mend is a repair, i.e. a fix
guys are men

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of sought

explanation.surface: Men who found themselves in trouble wanted things to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: A MEND and the final letter come together, and the guys go inside between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration, typically to a law or document, so a change.

clue.text: Literary princess lied so deviously

indicators.note: acting deviously means being twisty, so the letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A princess in a story told a lot of crafty lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan and Isolde legend, retold by Malory and set by Wagner.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the princess who loves Tristan in Arthurian romance, so a princess of literature.

clue.text: Bogus journalist discredited

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A fraudulent reporter has had their reputation ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamed means disgraced or brought into disrepute, so discredited.

clue.text: Retail customer ignoring the first jumper

indicators.note: ignoring the first means the opening letter is left out

parts.note: a shopper is a customer in a shop

explanation.surface: A shop customer who skips the queue and takes no notice of who was first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater, but here it means something that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopper is something that hops, such as a grasshopper or flea, so a creature that jumps.

clue.text: Lively pal kept providing moral-boosting words

indicators.note: lively letters jump about and land in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An energetic friend kept offering encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pep talk is a short speech meant to lift someone's spirits and confidence.

clue.text: Country pub, unpleasant and noisy from time to time

parts.note: a bar is a pub
bad means unpleasant

indicators.note: from time to time means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of noisy

explanation.surface: A rural pub that is grim and occasionally rowdy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country pub' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just Country.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an independent island nation in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Composer touring European holiday destination?

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: J.S. Bach, the German composer
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A composer on a European tour stops off at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach by the sea is a typical place to go on holiday, so this definition is by example.

clue.text: Try to contact young attendant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: summon over a tannoy or ...
second meaning: a boy servant or wedding attendant

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to reach a youthful helper.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to call them by pager or public address, and a page is a boy who attends a knight or a bride.

clue.text: Inexperienced soldiers overwhelmed by information

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being engulfed, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: New recruits swamped by briefings they cannot take in.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone new and untrained, so lacking experience.

clue.text: Court welcoming return of live discussion

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to court someone is to date them

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A courtroom resumes hearing a live argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb for wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion in which opposing arguments are put forward.

clue.text: Kid given lead part for the afternoon service?

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them

indicators.note: the lead part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the

explanation.surface: A child is cast in the main role for an afternoon church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church service; here it is a set of china, as in a dinner service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is a matching set of cups, saucers and pot, a service used for afternoon tea.

clue.text: Fastening made from odd bits of twine

indicators.note: odd bits are those in the first, third and fifth places

parts.note: letters one, three and five of twine

explanation.surface: A fastening improvised from scraps of string.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a cord or strip used to fasten or bind things together.

clue.text: Different things OKed for flexible work set-up

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager approves various changes to make office working more flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-desking is an office practice where staff have no fixed desk and use whichever is free.
